reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates TWIP/TRIP activation by carbon in a metastable dual-phase HEA, not in a single-phase BCC refractory alloy; the extrapolation to a BCC system and the specific carbon concentration are unsupported, and E3 highlights brittleness in related BCC/B2 systems without addressing interstitial effects.
premises: Interstitial carbon can activate TWIP/TRIP mechanisms in a BCC refractory high-entropy alloy
TWIP/TRIP mechanisms improve plasticity without reducing yield strength
A low carbon concentration (~0.3 at.%) is sufficient to trigger these mechanisms without forming carbides
The equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo alloy has a disordered BCC structure amenable to this approach
